c.tagline: Queen of the Arabian Sea — Chinese fishing nets, spice warehouses, and layers of colonial history.

taxi.fareNote: App cabs (Uber, Ola) are cheap and reliable on the mainland. Auto-rickshaws are everywhere and metered by law, but drivers often quote a flat fare — agree the price or insist on the meter before setting off, especially around Fort Kochi.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-services emergency number; 108 reaches a free state ambulance and 101 the fire service.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Auto-rickshaw drivers around Fort Kochi and Ernakulam may inflate fares or detour to commission shops — agree fares or use apps.

hood_desc: The atmospheric old peninsula of cantilevered Chinese fishing nets, Portuguese and Dutch colonial houses, St Francis Church, Kathakali theatres, and the Biennale art scene; the historic heart most visitors come for.

Just south of Fort Kochi, a warren of spice godowns, antique dealers along Jew Town, the 16th-century Paradesi Synagogue, and the mural-filled Mattancherry (Dutch) Palace; best for heritage browsing and shopping.
The busy commercial mainland across the harbour, centered on MG Road with malls, jewellers, restaurants, and the main railway and metro links; the practical, well-connected base for the modern city.
A landscaped waterfront promenade in Ernakulam facing the backwaters, lined with hotels, malls, and evening food stalls, with ferries and sunset boat cruises departing nearby; lively after dark.
A tranquil man-made island between Ernakulam and Fort Kochi holding the port, naval base, and a handful of waterfront resorts; calm and green, a quiet retreat close to the ferries.
lodging: The Fern Kochi, Series by Marriott

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; avoid tap water and street ice.

transit.pay: The Kochi Metro and the electric-boat Water Metro share the rechargeable Kochi1 card and QR tickets bought via the app; single metro fares run about ₹10–60 (US$0.12–0.70). City buses take cash, and auto-rickshaws and app cabs increasingly accept UPI/QR payments.
transit.hours: The metro runs roughly 6:00am to 10:00pm and Water Metro ferries from early morning to about 9:00pm; buses run late but frequency thins after dark, when app cabs and autos take over.
transit.note: Kochi spreads across islands and backwaters, so getting around blends the modern elevated Metro, the newer battery-powered Water Metro ferries, traditional passenger ferries, city buses, and ubiquitous auto-rickshaws.

transit.m: Prepaid taxi or app cab to Ernakulam/Fort Kochi (45–70 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants if no service charge is added; ₹50–100 for hotel porters and small rounding-up for auto and taxi drivers is appreciated.

landmarks: Chinese Fishing Nets (Cheena Vala)
Fort Kochi's shore-mounted cantilevered fishing nets, introduced centuries ago by Chinese traders, dip and rise at sunset in Kerala's most iconic silhouette.
Mattancherry Palace (Dutch Palace)
A 16th-century Portuguese-built palace renovated by the Dutch, famed for extraordinary Ramayana murals among the finest examples of Kerala's temple painting tradition.
Paradesi Synagogue and Jew Town
The Commonwealth's oldest active synagogue, built in 1568, glows with Belgian chandeliers and hand-painted Cantonese floor tiles amid antique-shop-lined Jew Town.
St. Francis Church
India's oldest European church, built in 1503, once held the tomb of Vasco da Gama, whose original gravesite remains marked inside.
Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica
Fort Kochi's pastel Indo-European basilica, rebuilt in 1905 on Portuguese foundations, dazzles with a lavishly frescoed interior and twin white spires.
Fort Kochi Beach and heritage quarter
Colonial bungalows, rain trees, and street art line this atmospheric seafront district where Portuguese, Dutch, and British layers mingle with fishing-boat bustle.
Kerala Kathakali Centre
An intimate Fort Kochi theater where visitors watch elaborate make-up rituals before nightly performances of Kathakali dance-drama, Kalaripayattu, and classical music.
Marine Drive, Ernakulam
Kochi's breezy backwater promenade faces the harbor's island-dotted panorama, best enjoyed on an evening stroll or a sunset ferry ride.
Hill Palace, Tripunithura
Kerala's largest archaeological museum fills the 49-building hilltop palace of the Cochin royal family with crown jewels, murals, and royal carriages.
Bolgatty Palace
A 1744 Dutch mansion turned heritage hotel on its own palm-fringed island, once the British Residency, evoking Kochi's layered colonial past.

train.note: No international trains. Ernakulam Junction and Ernakulam Town are the main stations, with a smaller stop at Cochin Harbour Terminus; long-distance services run north to Mumbai and Delhi and south to Thiruvananthapuram. Book on IRCTC 60 days ahead - the coastal Kerala routes are busy year-round and heavily so during Onam.

bus.note: No international coaches. KSRTC (https://www.keralartc.com/) runs from the Ernakulam KSRTC bus stand to Munnar, Alleppey, Thekkady and across Kerala, while private AC sleeper operators to Bengaluru and Chennai are bookable through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/). The Vyttila Mobility Hub is the main interchange for private long-distance coaches.

intl.op: Kerala State Water Transport Department — tickets at the jetty

intl.to: Alleppey & the Kerala backwaters (India) - all-day public backwater boat

ferry.note: There are no international sailings; the port takes cargo and cruise calls. The harbour ferries between Ernakulam, Fort Kochi and Vypin are cheap, frequent and much faster than the road, and the newer Kochi Water Metro runs modern electric boats on the same routes. The public boat down to Alleppey takes most of a day and is the budget alternative to a chartered houseboat.

half.name: Alleppey (Alappuzha)
half.blurb: Kerala's backwater hub, where houseboats drift along palm-fringed canals and lagoons through village life.

half.name: Kumarakom
half.blurb: A backwater village on Vembanad Lake with a bird sanctuary and traditional Kettuvallam houseboat cruises.

half.name: Athirappilly Falls
half.blurb: Kerala's largest waterfall, a wide curtain of water crashing through rainforest at the edge of the Sholayar range.

full.name: Munnar
full.blurb: A former colonial hill station in the Western Ghats, its slopes blanketed in rolling tea plantations and mist.

full.name: Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary (Thekkady)
full.blurb: A forested tiger reserve around an artificial lake, explored by boat safaris in search of elephants and wildlife.
